items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: That's the Bologna, Alphonse Pico composed that piece.

ctx.x: So everybody with the exception of Schilling and Philly Marsloff, but Marsloff wasn't in the brass band. Schilling took up ten of trombone. We got Eddie Riley, we got the two Dykemans, we got Roy Bridges, playing trap drums with us then. We formed a brass band and the brass band stuck, oh I guess in about 1909. The Fisher still had his band, he had Richie Brunus leading it, but he didn't go too far with it. What did Marsloff play? Marsloff's guitar. Paper hang about that, guitar play about that. And the Dyke…

T. Notchie Beg, uh, Lance composed that piece, and that was a real, real nigger piece. I mean, you talk about it as close to being colored. Manny Perez, he's dead in not quite a while, and he told Lance, he says, that was, he says, the most best nigger piece that I ever did here. He says, that really was a nigger piece. I tell you. And I said, oh, he just composed. Lance was pretty good. He was good. I still say, well, we used to have a three piece band, cornet, guitar, and bass. The brother band. And that was…
